title: Bulk Image Resizer
about: Bulk Image Resizer prepares a batch of supported images at once. It is designed for users who need consistent image dimensions across several files, with batch progress and a ZIP export workflow.
steps: Choose supported JPG, PNG, or WebP images in the upload area. Review the file limits shown by the workspace before selecting a large batch.
Set the output width and height or choose the available sizing mode. Keep aspect ratio enabled when you want to avoid stretching images.
Review the selected files and resize settings, then start the batch operation.
Wait for each file to finish processing and check the completed status and output dimensions.
Use the ZIP export control to download the processed batch. Open a few output files to verify dimensions and visual quality before using them.
capabilities: The registered workspace uses the browser Canvas API for image resizing and JSZip for client-side ZIP export. Supported inputs are JPEG, PNG, and WebP. Actual results depend on the selected dimensions, source images, browser support, and available device memory.
benefits: Batch processing can reduce repetitive work when preparing image sets for websites, product catalogs, documents, or social content. Applying one sizing rule to multiple images can help keep a collection consistent.
limitations: Resizing changes pixel dimensions and may change image quality or file size. Very large batches or high-resolution images can use substantial device memory. The workspace lists supported formats and limits; unsupported formats should be converted separately. Review output files before replacing originals.

faqs.question: Can I resize multiple images at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add multiple supported images, choose the sizing settings, process the batch, and export the completed files together when ZIP export is available.

faqs.question: Which formats are supported?
faqs.answer: The registered workspace accepts JPEG, PNG, and WebP images.

faqs.question: Will resizing stretch my images?
faqs.answer: Keep the aspect-ratio option enabled when you want to preserve the original proportions. Exact width and height without aspect-ratio locking can distort an image.

faqs.question: Are my images uploaded?
faqs.answer: The registered workflow uses the browser Canvas API and JSZip for client-side processing. Check the current privacy notice and workspace behavior before using sensitive files.

faqs.question: Why might a large batch fail?
faqs.answer: Browser memory and device resources can limit how many high-resolution images can be processed at once. Try smaller batches if the browser becomes unresponsive.
